1.why: All MFA endpoints go through auth() and bind solely to the session’s userId (account.id); client-supplied user identifiers are rejected by suppliedIdentifier().

2.why: OTP verification uses only this account’s pending/enabled secret; there is no behavior where one user’s code is accepted for a different user.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/verify only sets account.secret/enabled and does not invalidate or re-check existing entries in the sessions Map.

4.why: Pending/enabled OTP secrets are stored via encrypt() (AES-GCM); recovery codes store SHA-256 hashes plus AES-GCM ciphertext, not plaintext.

5.why: Secrets, session tokens, CSRF values, recovery codes, and base32 seeds all use crypto.getRandomValues (Web Crypto CSPRNG).

6.why: bank_session is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite; no code writes secrets, OTPs, or session tokens to localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email (emailOK), phone (phoneOK), OTP (/^\d{6}$/), recovery code format, JSON shape/size, and CSRF before acting.

8.why: Client esc() uses textContent for HTML insertion and CSP script/style is nonce-restricted, blocking injected markup/script execution.

9.why: No server redirect accepts user-controlled URLs; navigation is client hash-only to fixed internal steps, so open redirects are not possible.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY, and frame-ancestors 'none' on responses.

11.why: Set-Cookie for bank_session includes HttpOnly; Secure; and SameSite=Strict (and the same flags on logout clear).

12.why: The client deliberately logs provisioning secrets, test OTPs, and recovery codes into the on-page Logs panel and console, so they are not kept out of logs.

13.why: Pending OTP has expires (OTP_LIFE) and used flag enforced before accept; TOTP is step-windowed; recovery codes are marked used after redeem.

14.why: Failed OTP verify increments pending.attempts and locks for LOCK after 5 tries; recovery redeem similarly locks via failures/recoveryLocked.

15.why: Login deletes the prior cookie session and issues a new token; auth() enforces IDLE and ABSOLUTE timeouts; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
